subject: v1.1 task 11.1 - Inventory cache model, bounds, and limits (security re-review after correction round)

findings.summary: CLOSED-AS-DOCUMENTED. The documented contract now matches the actual guarantee: LastError is a bounded ArrProviderError whose value-level redaction is the producer contract, and the cache boundary explicitly does not redact it.
findings.issue: Attempt 1 recorded that ArrInventoryCacheEntry.LastError retained an ArrProviderError.Message verbatim and that secret-freedom rested on caller/producer convention rather than boundary enforcement. The correction round deliberately did not invent a new value-redaction policy; it made the documentation honest about the actual guarantee. Verified: (a) ArrInventoryCache remarks (src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCache.cs:19-24) state the boundary 'does not add value-level redaction and relies on that producer contract'; (b) ArrInventoryCacheEntry remarks (src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCacheEntry.cs:16-22) state the cache 'stores that value unchanged and does not perform value-level redaction of its message'; (c) docs/data-model.md section 6 (lines 1209-1213) states value-level redaction 'is the producer contract ... consistent with the per-item metadata record's last-error summary'; (d) docs/architecture.md section 12 (lines 1285-1290) states the same. The behavior is unchanged and still matches the docs: an independent probe confirmed a secret-bearing message is retained verbatim (so the docs are not overclaiming redaction). The cross-reference is accurate: MetadataStateEntry.LastError is also a producer-contract carrier with no boundary redaction (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataStateEntry.cs:133,273), and ADR-020 clause 4 explicitly lists ArrProviderError among the types 'already proven bounded and redacted'. Residual nuance (no action): the per-member XML summaries on ArrInventoryCacheEntry (constructor param :54, LastError :129, WithFailure :243,248) still use the word 'redacted' and rely on the reader reaching the class remarks for the producer-contract qualifier; this wording is identical to the pre-existing MetadataStateEntry.LastError wording and to ArrProviderError's own documented contract, so it is consistent rather than a new overstatement. With no caller yet (task 11.2 wires the producer), the resolution is sufficient for 11.1.
findings.description: The one free-text field is documented as a bounded ArrProviderError whose value-level redaction is the producer's responsibility; the cache does not claim boundary redaction and does not enforce it. findings.summary: UNCHANGED. InventoryCacheMaxBytes is enforced against a conservative estimate that omits several retained fields; the record-count bound remains the hard memory cap.
findings.issue: Attempt 1 recorded that EstimateSizeBytes sums UTF-16 lengths of a subset of canonical fields plus fixed overheads and omits BadgeMetadata.MetadataFingerprint, ArrRecordIdentity strings, ArrProvider strings, audio features, and object overhead, so actual retained bytes can exceed the configured byte bound by a bounded per-record amount. The correction round did not change the accounting (the worker report's known_limitations[2] continues to disclose it, and ByteBoundIsEnforcedAtTheActualEntrySize only pins the existing accounting boundary). This remains an accounting-accuracy gap, not unbounded growth: the record-count bound (<=100000) plus the counted variable strings keep memory bounded, and an over-bound store returns a safe false (direct-read fallback). No security action is required for 11.1.

findings.summary: CLOSED. The strengthened guard is non-vacuous: a member-type denylist over the cache object graph (including private fields) plus a bounded ArrProviderError contract assertion.
findings.issue: Attempt 1 recorded that the secret-free test was a non-recursive name heuristic that would not flag an innocuously-named secret-typed member. The correction renamed the heuristic to InventoryCacheTypesHaveNoSecretNamedMembers (explicitly marked secondary) and added InventoryCacheTypesExposeNoCredentialBearingMembers, which enumerates the member types (properties and private/public fields, unwrapping generics and arrays) of ArrInventoryCache, ArrInventoryCacheEntry, ArrInventoryRecordObservation, and ArrInventoryCacheState and rejects ArrConnection, ArrConnectionConfiguration, SecretReference, SecretLease, PluginConfiguration, MetadataStateEntry, and MetadataStateStore; it also asserts inspected > 0. Independently verified non-vacuous: the guard's enumeration covers private instance fields, and an isolated probe showed the same logic flags an innocuously-named property of type SecretLease and a private ArrConnection field. The new LastErrorSatisfiesTheBoundedRedactedProviderErrorContract asserts ArrProviderError.Message is truncated to MaxMessageLength and that ArrProviderError exposes exactly Code/Message/Retryability; it does not claim value redaction (consistent with the documented producer contract). Residual nuance (no action): the denylist is exact-type and does not recurse into nested canonical types (MatchCandidate/BadgeMetadata are pre-existing reviewed types), and SecretLease is sealed so exact-type matching is sufficient for it.
findings.description: The secret-free guard is now structural (member types, not names) and demonstrably catches a credential-typed member regardless of member name.

findings.summary: UNCHANGED. No cache-wide entry-count cap, but the live connection count is fixed at two.
findings.issue: ArrInventoryCache._entries is keyed by ArrConnectionId with no cap on distinct connections; ArrConnectionCatalog.FromSnapshot returns exactly two connections and V1 configures at most one per provider kind, so the live bound is two entries. findings.summary: UNCHANGED. observedAt is caller-supplied and not clamped to the store time.
findings.issue: ComputeFreshnessWindow derives ExpiresAt/StaleUntil from the caller-supplied observedAt; TryStore/TryGet do not reject a future observedAt, so a buggy caller passing a far-future observedAt would extend the freshness window. observedAt is the local provider read time (not attacker-influenced) and no caller exists yet.
findings.description: TTL is relative to the caller-supplied observation time, not the store time.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCacheEntry.cs:182-200 (freshness derived from observedAt)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrInventoryCache.cs:125-148 (TryStore accepts observedAt without a future check)
findings.recommended_action: No action for 11.1. Optional hardening at 11.2: clamp observedAt to the store time (or reject a future observedAt) so the TTL cannot be extended by a caller defect.

findings.summary: UNCHANGED. The cache retains raw provider strings as canonical observations but introduces no path/URL/log sink.
findings.issue: ArrInventoryRecordObservation retains provider-influenced strings (MatchCandidate.Title/PrimaryPath, provider ids, BadgeMetadata values). The cache performs no filesystem, URL, or log operation on them, so it adds no traversal/injection sink; BadgeMetadata already bounds custom badges and strips control characters, and MatchCandidate trims/normalizes provider ids. Task 11.2 must keep treating these values as untrusted and must not use PrimaryPath in a filesystem path, provider URL, or log line unescaped.

summary: Attempt-2 security re-review of v1.1 task 11.1 finds the cache genuinely secret-free and bounded for its actual data, non-authoritative, with no open BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM. SEC-11.1-1 is now closed-as-documented: the ArrInventoryCache/ArrInventoryCacheEntry remarks, docs/data-model.md section 6, and docs/architecture.md section 12 all state that LastError is a bounded ArrProviderError whose value-level redaction is the producer contract (ADR-020 clause 4), consistent with MetadataStateEntry.LastError, and the boundary explicitly does not redact; an independent probe confirmed the behavior matches (a secret-bearing message is retained verbatim), so no remaining claim overstates value-level redaction. SEC-11.1-3 is closed: the strengthened InventoryCacheTypesExposeNoCredentialBearingMembers guard is non-vacuous (member-type denylist over properties and private/public fields, unwrapping generics/arrays; independently demonstrated to catch an innocuously-named SecretLease property and a private ArrConnection field), and LastErrorSatisfiesTheBoundedRedactedProviderErrorContract asserts the bounded ArrProviderError contract without claiming value redaction. SEC-11.1-2 is unchanged (noted): InventoryCacheMaxBytes remains a conservative lower-bound estimate with the record-count bound as the hard cap, and the worker still discloses it. SEC-11.1-4/5/6 remain INFORMATIONAL/not_required. A transient credential-bearing private field was injected into the working tree during this review and reverted; it broke the build and was an exact denylist hit, which is recorded as SEC-11.1-7 (INFORMATIONAL) and as evidence that the correction's guard catches this class of regression. The final reviewed state builds with 0 warnings/0 errors, passes 24/24 focused and 1387/1450 default tests, and introduces no ETag/revision-token/SignalR dependency. Verdict: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS; the producer-contract obligation should be carried into task 11.2.
